lessons.title: What Is T-SQL? A Tour of SSMS
Connecting to a Database & the USE Statement

slots.practicalActivity: In SSMS, connect to the local SQL Server instance, open a new query window, and run USE AdventureWorks2012;. Expand Object Explorer's Tables node and note at least 8 real table names under the Person, Sales, and Production schemas. Write and run 3 SELECT TOP 10 * FROM queries against three different tables you found, watching the Results grid, the Messages tab, and the query execution time indicator each time.
slots.deliverable: A saved .sql script with 3 working SELECT TOP 10 * FROM queries against three different AdventureWorks2012 tables, each with a one-line comment noting its schema.

slots.practicalActivity: Write 5 original SELECT queries against AdventureWorks2012: 2 using SELECT * and 3 selecting specific named columns (at least 3 columns each) from Person.Person, Production.Product, and Sales.SalesOrderHeader.
slots.deliverable: A .sql file with 5 working SELECT queries, each run successfully in SSMS with visible results.

slots.practicalActivity: Write 4 queries against Person.Person that alias at least 2 columns each with AS, and build a full-name output by concatenating FirstName + ' ' + LastName (handling MiddleName with a trailing space) into a single aliased column called FullName.
slots.deliverable: 4 queries producing readable aliased column headers, including one FullName concatenation query.

slots.practicalActivity: Against Production.Product, write one simple CASE expression that translates the Color column into a friendlier label (e.g. 'N/A' for NULL), and one searched CASE expression that buckets ListPrice into 'Budget', 'Mid-range', and 'Premium' using comparison ranges.
slots.deliverable: 2 queries with working CASE expressions, each producing a new derived column in the result set.

slots.practicalActivity: Write 3 SELECT DISTINCT queries against Sales.SalesOrderHeader and Person.Person (e.g. distinct TerritoryID values, distinct City values), then reformat 3 of today's earlier queries with consistent capitalization, indentation, and a header comment block explaining what each query does.
slots.deliverable: 3 DISTINCT queries plus a cleaned-up, commented version of at least 3 earlier queries from this chapter.

slots.practicalActivity: Combine everything from Chapter 1, T-SQL Foundations, into a single statement: select specific aliased columns from Person.Person, concatenate a full name, add a CASE-based label column, and apply DISTINCT — all in one fully commented query.
slots.deliverable: One well-commented original query combining column aliasing, string concatenation, CASE, and DISTINCT in a single SELECT statement.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter-ending review for T-SQL Foundations: write 3 original queries from scratch (no looking back at lesson scripts) against Production.Product and Sales.SalesOrderHeader, each exercising a different combination of this chapter's skills — aliasing, concatenation, CASE, or DISTINCT — to confirm you can produce them without a reference.
slots.deliverable: 3 original, unaided queries demonstrating recall of SELECT basics, aliasing, concatenation, CASE, and DISTINCT.

slots.practicalActivity: Write 5 WHERE-clause queries against Sales.SalesOrderHeader and Production.Product using comparison operators (=, <>, >, <, >=, <=) to filter on OrderDate, TotalDue, and ListPrice.
slots.deliverable: 5 filtered queries, each returning a different subset of rows, with the row count noted in a comment for each.

slots.practicalActivity: Write 3 queries combining AND/OR/NOT conditions against Person.Person and Production.Product (e.g. products that are red OR blue AND under $500), then write 3 LIKE queries using %, _, and NOT LIKE against LastName or Name columns.
slots.deliverable: 6 queries demonstrating compound boolean filters and wildcard pattern matches.

lessons.title: Handling NULL (IS NULL / IS NOT NULL)

slots.practicalActivity: Write 2 IN queries and 2 BETWEEN queries against Sales.SalesOrderHeader (e.g. specific TerritoryIDs, OrderDate ranges), then write 2 queries using IS NULL / IS NOT NULL against Person.Person.MiddleName and Production.Product.Color.
slots.deliverable: 6 queries covering IN, BETWEEN, and NULL-safe filtering, each verified to return correct rows in SSMS.

slots.practicalActivity: Write 3 ORDER BY queries (ascending, descending, and multi-column sort) against Sales.SalesOrderHeader, then write 2 TOP queries (one TOP N, one TOP N PERCENT) to find the highest-value orders.
slots.deliverable: 5 queries demonstrating sorting and TOP/TOP PERCENT limiting on real order data.

lessons.title: Predicates: How SQL Server Filters Data

slots.practicalActivity: Find a column with duplicate values (e.g. ListPrice in Production.Product) and write a TOP WITH TIES query ordered by that column; then write 2 queries comparing how SQL Server evaluates predicates on an indexed column filter vs. a non-indexed column filter, using SET STATISTICS IO ON to see the difference.
slots.deliverable: A TOP WITH TIES query returning tied rows, plus 2 predicate-comparison queries with STATISTICS IO output captured.

slots.practicalActivity: Write one combined query against Sales.SalesOrderHeader that filters with a compound WHERE (AND/OR/IN/BETWEEN), handles NULLs safely, sorts the result, and returns only the TOP 10 WITH TIES — simulating a real 'top customers by order value' report.
slots.deliverable: One original multi-clause query combining filtering, NULL handling, sorting, and TOP WITH TIES, with a 2-sentence comment explaining the business question it answers.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter-ending review for Filtering and Sorting: without looking back at lesson examples, write 3 original queries against Person.Person and Production.Product from a short list of business questions you write yourself, each requiring a different filtering technique (LIKE, IN/BETWEEN, or NULL handling) plus sorting.
slots.deliverable: 3 original, unaided filter-and-sort queries, each preceded by the one-sentence business question it answers.

slots.practicalActivity: Identify the primary key and foreign key columns linking Sales.SalesOrderHeader to Sales.Customer and Person.Person using Object Explorer's Keys folders, then write 2 INNER JOIN queries: SalesOrderHeader to Customer, and Customer to Person, returning customer names with their order totals.
slots.deliverable: 2 INNER JOIN queries returning combined customer-and-order data, plus a short note identifying the PK/FK pair used in each join.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a LEFT JOIN from Production.Product to Sales.SalesOrderDetail to find products that have never been ordered (check for NULL on the right side), then rewrite the same logic as a RIGHT JOIN with the table order swapped to confirm it returns the same result set.
slots.deliverable: A LEFT JOIN query listing never-ordered products, plus an equivalent RIGHT JOIN query proving the same result from the opposite table order.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a FULL OUTER JOIN between two related AdventureWorks2012 tables to surface unmatched rows on both sides, then write a CROSS JOIN between a small distinct lookup set (e.g. distinct Sizes from Production.Product) and Production.Product to generate every combination, calculating the expected row count before running it.
slots.deliverable: A FULL OUTER JOIN showing unmatched rows from both tables, and a CROSS JOIN query whose actual row count you verify against your pre-calculated rows(A) x rows(B) estimate.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a SELF JOIN against a table with a self-referencing or hierarchical relationship in AdventureWorks2012 (e.g. Sales.SalesPerson territory structure) to pair related rows, then write a 3-table JOIN chaining Sales.SalesOrderHeader, Sales.SalesOrderDetail, and Production.Product to list order line items with real product names.
slots.deliverable: A working SELF JOIN query and a 3-table JOIN query returning order line items with real product names.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a CROSS APPLY query that, for each customer in Sales.Customer, returns their top 3 highest-value orders from Sales.SalesOrderHeader using a correlated TOP subquery inside the APPLY clause; then convert it to OUTER APPLY and compare which customers (if any) with zero orders now appear.
slots.deliverable: A CROSS APPLY 'top-3-orders-per-customer' query and its OUTER APPLY variant, with a one-line comparison of the row-count difference.

slots.practicalActivity: For 4 different business questions you write yourself (e.g. 'all products and whether they've sold', 'every order with customer info', 'all possible product/territory pairs for planning'), decide which join type fits each and write the query, annotating each with a comment justifying the join choice.
slots.deliverable: 4 queries, each preceded by a comment explaining why that specific join type (INNER/LEFT/CROSS/etc.) was the right choice for the question.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter-ending lab for Joining Tables: without looking back at lesson examples, write an original 5-table join query from scratch (SalesOrderHeader, SalesOrderDetail, Product, Customer, Person) that lists, for every order, the customer's full name, product name, quantity, and line total — deliberately choosing INNER vs. LEFT JOIN for each relationship and documenting the choice in comments.
slots.deliverable: One original 5-table join lab query with full comments justifying each join type, executed successfully with results visible in SSMS.

slots.practicalActivity: Combine a standard JOIN with CROSS APPLY in a single query: JOIN Sales.SalesTerritory to Sales.SalesOrderHeader, then use CROSS APPLY to pull each territory's single highest-value order, closing out the chapter with the APPLY pattern in a realistic report shape.
slots.deliverable: One query combining a standard JOIN with CROSS APPLY to answer 'what is the highest-value order per sales territory'.

slots.practicalActivity: Write 2 COUNT queries (COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT column)) against Sales.SalesOrderDetail, and 2 SUM/AVG queries computing the total and average LineTotal across the whole table.
slots.deliverable: 4 aggregate queries returning single summary numbers from real order-detail data.

slots.practicalActivity: Write MIN/MAX queries finding the cheapest and most expensive product in Production.Product, then write 3 single-column GROUP BY queries: total sales per ProductID, order count per CustomerID, and average price per ProductSubcategoryID.
slots.deliverable: 2 MIN/MAX queries and 3 single-column GROUP BY aggregate queries.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a GROUP BY query grouping Sales.SalesOrderDetail by both ProductID and SpecialOfferID, then write 2 queries contrasting HAVING (filtering on the aggregate, e.g. products with total quantity sold > 500) vs. WHERE (filtering rows before aggregation) on the same data.
slots.deliverable: A multi-column GROUP BY query plus a side-by-side WHERE-vs-HAVING comparison on the same aggregate.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a UNION query combining two differently-filtered SELECTs from Sales.SalesOrderHeader (e.g. big orders and small orders) and the same query as UNION ALL, comparing row counts and duplicate handling; then write a VAR/STDEV query on SalesOrderHeader.TotalDue.
slots.deliverable: A UNION and UNION ALL pair showing the duplicate-removal difference, plus one VAR/STDEV statistical query.

slots.practicalActivity: Build an original summary-report query combining GROUP BY, HAVING, and at least 2 aggregate functions to answer: 'which product subcategories had total sales over a threshold you choose, ranked by total descending?'
slots.deliverable: One polished summary-report query with GROUP BY, HAVING, and ORDER BY producing a ranked business report.

slots.practicalActivity: Write an original sales-summary report from scratch, joining Sales.SalesOrderHeader to Sales.SalesOrderDetail and Production.Product, grouping by product category, using COUNT/SUM/AVG together, filtering groups with HAVING, and sorting the final report — combining joins with aggregation.
slots.deliverable: One original multi-table aggregate report query combining joins, GROUP BY, HAVING, and multiple aggregate functions.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter-ending review for Grouping and Aggregating: write 2 original queries from a business question you write yourself, each requiring GROUP BY plus at least 2 aggregate functions, without referring back to lesson examples.
slots.deliverable: 2 original, unaided aggregate queries, each stating the business question it answers in a comment.

slots.practicalActivity: Inspect the column data types of Person.Person via Object Explorer's table Design view or sys.columns, noting which columns use CHAR, VARCHAR, and NVARCHAR; then write 2 queries returning DATALENGTH() of a name column to compare single-byte vs. Unicode storage.
slots.deliverable: 2 DATALENGTH queries on real columns, plus written notes on which AdventureWorks2012 columns use CHAR vs. VARCHAR vs. NVARCHAR.

slots.practicalActivity: Find a VARCHAR(MAX) column in Production.ProductDescription and run a query returning its DATALENGTH() alongside a few short VARCHAR columns to see the storage difference; then write 2 queries using LEN, UPPER, and LOWER on Person.Person.LastName.
slots.deliverable: A VARCHAR(MAX) DATALENGTH comparison query, plus 2 LEN/UPPER/LOWER queries against real name data.

slots.practicalActivity: Write 2 SUBSTRING/CHARINDEX queries that dynamically extract a segment of a ProductNumber code by finding the position of its '-' separator; then write a STUFF query that masks part of a text value and a REPLACE query that swaps a character in Production.Product.Name.
slots.deliverable: 2 SUBSTRING/CHARINDEX queries plus a STUFF vs. REPLACE comparison pair, all against real Production.Product data.

slots.practicalActivity: Write 3 TRIM/LTRIM/RTRIM queries cleaning whitespace from a concatenated text column, proving the before/after difference with LEN(); then query sys.columns to find 3 date/time columns in Sales.SalesOrderHeader and note their exact data types (DATETIME vs. DATE vs. SMALLDATETIME).
slots.deliverable: 3 trimming queries with LEN()-verified before/after whitespace proof, plus a written list of 3 real date/time columns and their types.

slots.practicalActivity: Write 4 GETDATE/DATEADD/DATEDIFF queries computing order age in days, a projected ship date, and orders placed within the last 30 days relative to the dataset's latest OrderDate; then write 3 CAST/CONVERT queries reformatting OrderDate into different string styles and converting a numeric column to varchar for concatenation.
slots.deliverable: 4 date-function queries including a DATEDIFF-based 'days since order' calculation, plus 3 CAST/CONVERT formatting queries.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a scratch temp table with intentionally duplicated rows (copy a few rows from Person.Person twice) and write a dedup query using ROW_NUMBER() PARTITION BY the duplicate columns, deleting every row where the row number is greater than 1.
slots.deliverable: One working duplicate-removal query tested against a temp table with real duplicate rows, with before/after row counts noted.

slots.practicalActivity: Build one original data-cleaning query for Chapter 5: pull Person.Person names, TRIM any whitespace, UPPER-case the last name, concatenate a formatted full name, CONVERT a date column to 'yyyy-mm-dd' string format, and use SUBSTRING to pull the first 3 characters of a phone number — all in one SELECT.
slots.deliverable: One combined string/date-cleaning query exercising at least 5 different functions from this chapter.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter-ending review for Data Types, Strings, and Dates: without looking back, write 2 original queries from scratch that each combine a string function and a date function against real AdventureWorks2012 columns of your choosing.
slots.deliverable: 2 original, unaided queries each combining one string function and one date function.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a single-value (scalar) subquery finding all products priced above the average ListPrice, then write a multi-value subquery using IN to find all orders placed by customers in a specific list of territories returned by a subquery against Sales.SalesTerritory.
slots.deliverable: A scalar-subquery 'above average price' query and a multi-value IN subquery query.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a correlated subquery that returns each customer's most recent order date inline per row, then write an EXISTS query finding customers who have placed at least one order over $5,000, and a NOT EXISTS query finding products never ordered.
slots.deliverable: One correlated subquery and two EXISTS/NOT EXISTS queries, each verified against known AdventureWorks2012 data.

slots.practicalActivity: Rewrite one of your earlier subquery solutions as a CTE for readability, then write a recursive CTE that walks the Production.ProductCategory/ProductSubcategory hierarchy to list parent-child levels.
slots.deliverable: A readable CTE rewrite of a prior query, plus a working recursive CTE traversing a real hierarchy in AdventureWorks2012.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a view named vw_CustomerOrderSummary that joins Customer, Person, and SalesOrderHeader to show each customer's order count and total spend, then query it like a table; research via sys.indexes whether an indexed view would suit this case and explain why or why not in a comment.
slots.deliverable: A working CREATE VIEW statement, a SELECT against that view, and a written note on indexed-view suitability.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a PIVOT query turning Sales.SalesOrderHeader order counts by TerritoryID into columns, one column per territory, with order years as rows; then write an UNPIVOT query that reshapes that same result back into a tall/normalized format, confirming the row count matches the original pre-pivot data.
slots.deliverable: One working PIVOT query reshaping territory-by-year order data into a cross-tab, plus an UNPIVOT query reversing it back to normalized rows.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter-ending lab for Subqueries, CTEs, and Views: build one query that uses a CTE to pre-aggregate order totals per customer, uses EXISTS against that CTE to filter to customers above a threshold, then PIVOTs the result by order year — combining CTEs, EXISTS, and PIVOT in a single original multi-step query.
slots.deliverable: One original multi-technique query chaining a CTE, an EXISTS filter, and a PIVOT, successfully executed in SSMS.

slots.practicalActivity: Solve the same business question — 'which customers have above-average total spend' — three different ways: once with a correlated subquery, once with a CTE, and once by querying a view you create for it. Compare the three queries' readability in a short note.
slots.deliverable: Three functionally-equivalent queries (subquery, CTE, view-based) answering the same question, with a short written comparison of readability and maintainability.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a script that DECLAREs 3 variables of different types (INT, VARCHAR, DATETIME), assigns values with SELECT/SET, and PRINTs a formatted message using them; split the script into 2 batches with GO and confirm the variables don't persist across the GO boundary.
slots.deliverable: A script demonstrating variable declaration and use, plus proof (via an error or empty result) that GO resets variable scope.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a script that stores a real product's ListPrice (via SELECT INTO a variable) and uses IF/ELSE with BEGIN/END blocks to PRINT different messages for 'budget', 'mid-range', and 'premium' price tiers.
slots.deliverable: A working IF/ELSE/BEGIN/END script that branches based on a real queried value.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a WHILE loop that prints the numbers 1-10 with a running total, then write a cursor that iterates over the top 5 highest-priced products in Production.Product and PRINTs each product's name and price one row at a time.
slots.deliverable: A working WHILE loop script and a working cursor script that iterates real product rows.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a stored procedure usp_GetCustomerOrders that takes a @CustomerID parameter and returns that customer's orders from Sales.SalesOrderHeader, with a default parameter value and an OUTPUT parameter returning the order count; then EXEC it with 2 different customer IDs.
slots.deliverable: A working CREATE PROCEDURE with input and OUTPUT parameters, executed successfully with 2 different inputs.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a dynamic SQL script using sp_executesql that builds a SELECT statement where the filter column's value is chosen based on a variable, using parameterized dynamic SQL (not string concatenation) to avoid injection risk; then create a small staging temp table with a few changed and new product rows and write a MERGE statement that syncs it into a scratch copy of Production.Product.
slots.deliverable: One working sp_executesql script with properly parameterized dynamic SQL, plus a working MERGE statement with INSERT and UPDATE actions tested against a staging table.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter-ending lab for Programming with T-SQL: build one original stored procedure that accepts a @MinTotal parameter, uses IF/ELSE to validate it, and returns orders above that total using proper BEGIN/END and parameter handling — then EXEC it twice with different threshold values.
slots.deliverable: One original parameterized stored procedure combining variables, IF/ELSE, and BEGIN/END, executed with 2 different parameter values.

slots.practicalActivity: On a scratch copy of a small table, write a script using BEGIN TRANSACTION, make an UPDATE, verify the change inside the transaction, then ROLLBACK and verify it reverted; repeat with COMMIT and verify the change persists. Write one sentence per ACID property explaining how this demo illustrated it.
slots.deliverable: A working transaction script demonstrating both ROLLBACK and COMMIT outcomes, plus 4 short written ACID explanations tied to the demo.

slots.practicalActivity: Open two SSMS query windows against the same scratch table: in window 1, start a transaction with an UPDATE but don't commit; in window 2, try to SELECT or UPDATE the same rows and observe the blocking; use sp_who2 or sys.dm_tran_locks to inspect the lock held, then COMMIT window 1 and confirm window 2 unblocks.
slots.deliverable: A documented two-session blocking demo with notes on the lock type observed and how it resolved.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a TRY/CATCH block around an intentionally failing statement (e.g. an INSERT violating a constraint), capturing ERROR_MESSAGE/ERROR_NUMBER in the CATCH block; then write a script using RAISERROR and one using THROW to raise a custom business-rule error.
slots.deliverable: A working TRY/CATCH script that captures a real error, plus one RAISERROR and one THROW example raising custom errors.

slots.practicalActivity: In SSMS's connection dialog, examine the difference between Windows Authentication and SQL Server Authentication options; query sys.server_principals to list the login accounts and their authentication type on your instance, and write a short note on when you'd choose each mode in a real deployment.
slots.deliverable: A query result listing server logins by auth type, plus a short written recommendation for a given deployment scenario.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter-ending review for Transactions and Error Handling: write one script combining a transaction, TRY/CATCH, and THROW — attempt an UPDATE inside BEGIN TRANSACTION, deliberately trigger a constraint violation, catch it, ROLLBACK inside the CATCH block, and THROW a custom re-raised error with a clear message.
slots.deliverable: One original script combining transactions, TRY/CATCH, ROLLBACK, and THROW into a safe error-handling pattern.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a query using OVER(PARTITION BY TerritoryID) to show each order's TotalDue alongside the average TotalDue for its territory; then write a ROW_NUMBER() query numbering each customer's orders from most recent to oldest, partitioned by CustomerID.
slots.deliverable: A PARTITION BY aggregate-window query and a ROW_NUMBER() per-customer ordering query.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a query ranking products by ListPrice within each ProductSubcategoryID using both RANK() and DENSE_RANK(), comparing how they handle tied prices; then write an NTILE(4) query splitting customers into spending quartiles based on total order value.
slots.deliverable: A side-by-side RANK vs. DENSE_RANK query showing tie behavior, plus an NTILE(4) quartile-assignment query.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter-ending lab for Window and Ranking Functions: build an original 'top 3 products per category by sales' report using ROW_NUMBER() PARTITION BY category ORDER BY total sales descending inside a CTE, filtering WHERE rn <= 3 in the outer query — a classic real-world window-function pattern.
slots.deliverable: One original top-N-per-group report query using a window function inside a CTE, correctly limited to the top 3 rows per category.

lessons.title: The Cartesian Product: What Happens When Joins Go Wrong

slots.practicalActivity: Write a baseline query against Sales.SalesOrderDetail and time it using SSMS's query execution time; then deliberately write a query that omits the JOIN condition between two tables to produce an accidental Cartesian product, observe the exploded row count, then fix it by adding the correct ON clause.
slots.deliverable: A timed baseline query, plus a before/after pair showing an accidental Cartesian product and its corrected join.

lessons.title: Joins vs. Subqueries: Which Is Faster, and Why
EXISTS vs. IN vs. JOIN for Existence Checks

slots.practicalActivity: Write the question 'customers with at least one order over $5,000' three ways: as a JOIN with DISTINCT, as an IN subquery, and as an EXISTS subquery; turn on Include Actual Execution Plan and compare the plans and relative costs of all three.
slots.deliverable: Three functionally-equivalent queries (JOIN, IN, EXISTS) with execution-plan cost notes comparing them.

lessons.title: Clustered vs. Nonclustered Indexes: Choosing Wisely

slots.practicalActivity: Write a non-SARGable query (e.g. WHERE YEAR(OrderDate) = 2013) and a SARGable rewrite (WHERE OrderDate >= '2013-01-01' AND OrderDate < '2014-01-01') against Sales.SalesOrderHeader, comparing execution plans; then use Object Explorer to identify the clustered vs. nonclustered indexes on that table.
slots.deliverable: A non-SARGable/SARGable query pair with plan comparison, plus a written list of the table's clustered and nonclustered indexes.

lessons.title: Reading Execution Plans: Scans vs. Seeks

slots.practicalActivity: Create a filtered index on Sales.SalesOrderHeader for a narrow condition (e.g. WHERE Status = 5) with an included column, then write a query that benefits from it and confirm via the execution plan that the filtered index is used (Index Seek) rather than a full scan.
slots.deliverable: A CREATE INDEX statement (filtered, with INCLUDE), plus execution-plan notes confirming an Index Seek on it.

lessons.title: SET STATISTICS TIME and IO in Practice

slots.practicalActivity: Turn on SET STATISTICS TIME ON and SET STATISTICS IO ON, run 2 versions of the same query (one aided by an index, one forced to scan), and compare CPU time and logical reads; then capture the XML execution plan for one of them.
slots.deliverable: Before/after STATISTICS TIME/IO output comparing two query versions, plus one captured XML execution plan.

lessons.title: Temp Tables vs. Table Variables vs. CTEs: Performance Tradeoffs

slots.practicalActivity: Solve the same multi-step aggregation problem three ways: once staging intermediate results in a #temp table, once in a table variable, and once in a CTE, comparing execution plans; then find and fix 3 performance anti-patterns in queries you wrote earlier in this course (e.g. SELECT *, a non-SARGable WHERE, a scalar function on a filtered column) by rewriting each one.
slots.deliverable: Three equivalent query solutions (temp table, table variable, CTE) with written performance notes, plus 3 before/after anti-pattern fixes with plan or STATISTICS IO evidence of improvement.

slots.practicalActivity: Take your Chapter 3 five-table join lab query (or a similarly complex query from earlier), run it with Actual Execution Plan on, identify the most expensive operator, and rewrite the query to reduce its cost — documenting the specific change and the before/after cost percentages.
slots.deliverable: One documented query optimization: original query, its most expensive plan operator identified, the rewritten query, and a before/after cost comparison.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter-ending review for Performance Tuning: pick 2 queries from earlier chapters and apply the full tuning checklist from this chapter to each — check SARGability, index usage, anti-patterns, and compare a temp-table/CTE approach — writing a short tuning report for each with a final optimization recommendation.
slots.deliverable: A short written tuning report for 2 prior queries, each covering SARGability, index usage, and a final optimization recommendation.

slots.practicalActivity: Run EXEC sp_helpconstraint 'Production.Product'; to confirm its real primary key, then create your own dbo.Lesson95Demo table with an inline PRIMARY KEY and a composite-key table modeled on Sales.SalesOrderDetail's (SalesOrderID, SalesOrderDetailID) pattern; then create a second scratch table with a FOREIGN KEY referencing it and prove with an INSERT that an invalid reference is rejected.
slots.deliverable: A composite-primary-key scratch table plus a second table with a working FOREIGN KEY constraint, with a rejected invalid INSERT captured as proof.

slots.practicalActivity: Add a UNIQUE constraint to a non-key column on a scratch table (e.g. an email address column) and prove a duplicate INSERT is rejected; then add a NOT NULL column and a CHECK constraint (e.g. Price >= 0) to the same table and prove both a NULL insert and a negative-price insert are rejected.
slots.deliverable: One scratch table with UNIQUE, NOT NULL, and CHECK constraints, each proven to reject an invalid INSERT.

slots.practicalActivity: Query the real one-to-one relationship between Person.Person and HumanResources.Employee (JOIN on BusinessEntityID, which is both PK and FK on the Employee side) and confirm with COUNT(*) that every Employee matches exactly one Person; then write a one-to-many query from Sales.SalesOrderHeader to its many Sales.SalesOrderDetail rows and count detail rows per order.
slots.deliverable: A verified one-to-one Person/Employee query with matching row counts, plus a one-to-many SalesOrderHeader/SalesOrderDetail query showing detail-row counts per order.

slots.practicalActivity: Query the real many-to-many junction table Sales.SalesOrderHeaderSalesReason, joining Sales.SalesOrderHeader and Sales.SalesReason to list every reason cited for a specific order, then GROUP BY reason to count how often each is cited across all orders; then write a short note identifying one AdventureWorks2012 column that respects 1NF (atomic values) and explain why a comma-separated list in a single column would violate it.
slots.deliverable: A many-to-many junction-table query plus a reason-citation count query, and a written 1NF explanation using a real column as the example.

slots.practicalActivity: Design (on paper or in a comment block) a small denormalized order table with repeating customer and product attributes, then show how splitting it into Customer, Product, and OrderDetail tables resolves the 2NF/3NF partial and transitive dependencies; then in SSMS's Object Explorer, expand System Databases and write one sentence each on what master, msdb, tempdb, and model are used for.
slots.deliverable: A written before/after normalization example (denormalized table split into 2NF/3NF-compliant tables), plus one sentence per system database explaining its purpose.

slots.practicalActivity: In one SSMS query window create a #local and a ##global temp table and insert a row into each; open a second query window (new session) and prove the #local table is invisible there while the ##global table is visible and queryable; then right-click your server in Object Explorer, start an XEvent Profiler trace, run a couple of queries, and note which columns of the live trace match Duration/CPU/Reads from Chapter 10's STATISTICS tools.
slots.deliverable: A two-session local-vs-global temp table proof (one query failing, one succeeding across sessions), plus a short note mapping XEvent Profiler trace columns to Chapter 10's per-query metrics.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter-ending review for Database Design Fundamentals: design an original small schema (3-4 tables, on paper or as CREATE TABLE statements) for a made-up scenario of your choosing, correctly applying primary keys, foreign keys, at least one CHECK constraint, and a junction table if a many-to-many relationship is needed — then write one sentence confirming it satisfies 3NF.
slots.deliverable: An original 3-4 table schema design (CREATE TABLE statements or a written ER description) with PK/FK/CHECK constraints and a 3NF justification.

lessons.title: OLTP vs. OLAP: Two Different Worlds

slots.practicalActivity: Connect to both AdventureWorks2012 (OLTP) and AdventureWorksDW2014 (warehouse) in SSMS and write 1 query against each: a single-row INSERT-style lookup against AdventureWorks2012's Sales.SalesOrderHeader (the kind of fast point lookup OLTP is built for), and a large aggregate query against AdventureWorksDW2014's dbo.FactInternetSales summing SalesAmount by year (the kind of broad scan OLAP is built for); write 2 sentences contrasting what each system optimizes for.
slots.deliverable: One OLTP-style point-lookup query and one OLAP-style aggregate query against the two real databases, with a 2-sentence written contrast of what each optimizes for.

slots.practicalActivity: Looking at AdventureWorksDW2014's table list in Object Explorer, identify which tables would belong to a narrower 'Sales data mart' subset versus the full warehouse, and write that subset list out; then write a short note describing what raw, unprocessed source files (e.g. the original AdventureWorks2012 OLTP exports) would look like sitting in a data lake before being transformed into the warehouse's dimensional tables.
slots.deliverable: A written data-mart table subset list from AdventureWorksDW2014, plus a short note describing the same data's raw form in a data lake before transformation.

lessons.title: Data Warehouse vs. Data Lake vs. Data Mart

slots.practicalActivity: Draw (in a comment block or on paper) a 3-box diagram showing data lake to data warehouse to data mart, labeling what narrows at each step; then write out the same AdventureWorks2012-to-AdventureWorksDW2014 pipeline as an ETL sequence (extract raw OrderHeader/OrderDetail rows, transform into FactInternetSales shape, load into the warehouse) versus how it would differ as ELT.
slots.deliverable: A written lake-to-warehouse-to-mart diagram description, plus a side-by-side ETL vs. ELT sequence for the same AdventureWorks2012-to-warehouse pipeline.

slots.practicalActivity: Against AdventureWorksDW2014, run SELECT COUNT(*) on dbo.FactInternetSales and dbo.DimProduct to see the tall-fact/short-dimension shape for yourself; then write the real 4-dimension star-schema query joining FactInternetSales to DimDate, DimProduct, DimCustomer, and DimSalesTerritory, summing SalesAmount grouped by product name and territory region.
slots.deliverable: A fact/dimension row-count comparison query, plus a working 4-table star-schema query producing a sales-by-product-and-territory report.

slots.practicalActivity: Inspect AdventureWorksDW2014's DimProductSubcategory and DimProductCategory tables and write a query joining DimProduct to DimProductSubcategory to DimProductCategory — two hops instead of star schema's one — to see a real snowflaked dimension; then query DimProduct's real StartDate/EndDate/Status columns to find products that have been through a Type 2 slowly-changing-dimension change, using GROUP BY ProductAlternateKey HAVING COUNT(*) > 1.
slots.deliverable: A 2-hop snowflaked dimension join query, plus a Type 2 SCD query finding products with more than one DimProduct version.

lessons.title: Where T-SQL Fits in the BI/Warehousing Pipeline

slots.practicalActivity: Query DimProduct to see ProductKey (the surrogate key, a meaningless warehouse-generated integer) alongside ProductAlternateKey (the natural key carried over from AdventureWorks2012's real ProductID), and write 2 sentences on why the warehouse needs its own surrogate key even though a natural key already exists; then write a short closing summary mapping which T-SQL skill from each of this course's 12 chapters would be used at which stage of a real BI pipeline (extraction queries, staging transforms, warehouse loads, and reporting views).
slots.deliverable: A surrogate-vs-natural-key comparison query with written reasoning, plus a 12-chapter skill-to-pipeline-stage summary closing out the course.

slots.practicalActivity: Capstone review for Data Warehouse Concepts and the full course: build one original report query against AdventureWorksDW2014 that joins FactInternetSales to at least 3 dimension tables, uses a window function (ROW_NUMBER or RANK) to rank results within a group, and filters using a technique from an earlier chapter (CTE, EXISTS, or HAVING) — demonstrating that OLTP-chapter skills transfer directly to warehouse querying.
slots.deliverable: One original capstone query against AdventureWorksDW2014 combining a 3+ table star-schema join, a window function, and at least one filtering technique from an earlier chapter.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: After this course, a student can write real, correct T-SQL end to end against a live SQL Server database — filtering, joining, grouping, subqueries and CTEs, stored procedures, transactions with proper error handling, window functions, and index-aware performance tuning — and can explain and query a star-schema data warehouse, the foundation every later Azure Database Engineer course builds on.
